earnings_release.text: EX-99.1 2 cbre-20261022x8kexx991.htm EX-99.1 Document EXHIBIT 99.1 Press Release FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE For further information: Chandni Luthra - Investors Steve Iaco - Media 212.984.8113 212.984.6535 Chandni.Luthra@cbre.com Steven.Iaco@cbre.com CBRE GROUP, INC. REPORTS FINANCIAL RESULTS FOR Q3 2026 Dallas – October 22, 2026 — CBRE Group, Inc. (NYSE: CBRE) today reported financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. Key Highlights: • GAAP EPS up 26% to $1.52 and Core EPS up 28% to $2.05 • Revenue up 13% to $11.5 billion • Infrastructure services revenue up 50% to $4.5 billion on a trailing 12-month basis • Cash flow from operations of $1.4 billion and free cash flow of $1.8 billion, both on a trailing 12-month basis “CBRE produced another quarter of strong financial results and continued to make strategic gains in targeted areas of our business,” said Bob Sulentic, CBRE’s chair and chief executive officer. “Financially, core earnings per share improved 28% on a 13% revenue increase, with both resilient (1) and transactional (1) businesses growing by double digits. Strategically, we continued to advance both our Critical Infrastructure Services business line as well as the broader infrastructure services work we perform across the company.” CBRE Press Release October 22, 2026 Page 2 Consolidated Financial Results Overview The following table presents highlights of CBRE performance (dollars in millions, except per share data): % Change Q3 2026 Q3 2025 USD LC ( 2 ) Operating Results Revenue $ 11,517 $ 10,221 12.7 % 12.9 % Pass-through costs (3) 4,691 4,212 11.4 % 11.8 % GAAP net income 443 363 22.0 % 23.4 % Core adjusted net income (4) 599 481 24.5 % 25.6 % GAAP EPS 1.52 1.21 25.6 % 27.3 % Core EPS (4) 2.05 1.60 28.1 % 29.4 % Core EBITDA (5) 1,001 779 28.5 % 29.1 % Cash Flow Results Cash flow provided by operations $ 869 $ 827 5.1 % Gain on disposition of real estate 184 36 411.1 % Less: Capital expenditures 126 84 50.0 % Free cash flow (6) $ 927 $ 779 19.0 % Advisory Services Segment The following table presents highlights of the Advisory Services segment performance (dollars in millions): % Change Q3 2026 Q3 2025 USD LC Revenue $ 2,441 $ 2,199 11.0% 11.2% Pass-through costs 16 14 14.3% 14.3% Segment operating profit (7) 467 403 15.9% 16.4% • Revenue and segment operating profit increased by 11% (same local currency) and 16% (same local currency), respectively. • Global leasing revenue increased 6% (same local currency). EMEA revenue grew 21% (22% local currency), driven by the U.K. U.S. revenue rose 4% overall, led by industrial, up 16%, while office was down 2%. APAC revenue was up 2% (same local currency). • Global property sales revenue rose 28% (29% local currency). U.S. revenue was up 37%, driven by accelerated growth in industrial and retail. APAC revenue rose 10% (14% local currency), while EMEA revenue grew 8% (9% local currency). • Mortgage origination revenue edged up 1% (same local currency). Increased activity with private capital sources was largely offset by lower government agency lending. • The loan servicing portfolio rose 8% during the quarter to more than $500 billion. Revenue was down slightly as lower escrow income offset higher loan servicing fees. • Valuations revenue rose 6% (same local currency), driven by the U.S. CBRE Press Release October 22, 2026 Page 3 Building Operations & Experience (BOE) Segment The following table presents highlights of the BOE segment performance (dollars in millions): % Change Q3 2026 Q3 2025 USD LC Revenue $ 6,856 $ 5,842 17.4% 17.5% Pass-through costs 3,641 3,118 16.8% 17.1% Segment operating profit 349 289 20.8% 21.1% • Revenue and segment operating profit increased by 17% (18% local currency) and 21% (same local currency), respectively. • Revenue from critical infrastructure services surged 80% (same local currency), driven by continued strong growth in data center services solutions and contributions from Pearce Services, acquired in November 2025. • Facilities management revenue rose 13% (same local currency). Solid double-digit growth was achieved in both the enterprise business, led by technology, financial services and energy clients, and the local business, driven by the Americas, Asia Pacific and Western Europe. • Property management revenue rose 8% (same local currency). Project Management Segment The following table presents highlights of the Project Management segment performance (dollars in millions): % Change Q3 2026 Q3 2025 USD LC Revenue $ 2,035 $ 1,978 2.9% 3.2% Pass-through costs 1,034 1,080 (4.3)% (3.8)% Segment operating profit 162 148 9.5% 9.5% • Revenue increased by 3% (same local currency), while pass-through costs declined 4% (same local currency). • Growth was driven by continued strong demand for program management and cost consulting services for infrastructure assets. • The overall growth rate was tempered by a slowdown in corporate capital spending on real estate. • Segment operating profit increased 9% (10% local currency), including a one-time cost in APAC that lowered the growth rate by six percentage points. CBRE Press Release October 22, 2026 Page 4 Real Estate Investments (REI) Segment The following table presents highlights of the REI segment performance (dollars in millions): % Change Q3 2026 Q3 2025 USD LC Revenue $ 203 $ 211 (3.8) % (2.8) % Segment operating profit 166 73 127.4 % 128.8 % Real Estate Development • Operating profit (8) totaled $128 million, up significantly from the third quarter of 2025, reflecting strong data center land sale activity and monetization of other assets. • The portfolio of in-process projects and pipeline ended the third quarter at $29.6 billion, unchanged from the second quarter. Excluding fee development, the overall portfolio stands at $20.2 billion. Investment Management • Revenue increased 4% (5% local currency), reflecting higher recurring asset management fees as well as increased incentive fees. • Operating profit (8) totaled $38 million, down from third-quarter 2025. Higher asset management fees were offset by lower co-investment returns. • Assets under management (AUM) ended the third quarter at more than $155 billion. Core Corporate Segment Core corporate operating loss increased by approximately $9 million for the quarter, primarily driven by higher incentive compensation, reflecting the company’s strong performance in 2026. Capital Allocation Overview • Free Cash Flow – Free cash flow totaled $1.8 billion for the 12 months ended September 30, 2026. • Stock Repurchase Program – Year-to-date, the company repurchased nearly $1.2 billion worth of shares. CBRE Press Release October 22, 2026 Page 5 Leverage and Financing Overview • Leverage – CBRE’s net leverage ratio (net debt (9) to trailing twelve-month core EBITDA) was 1.36x as of September 30, 2026. The net leverage ratio is computed as follows (dollars in millions): As of September 30, 2026 Total debt $ 6,978 Less: Cash and cash equivalents 1,683 Net debt (9) $ 5,295 Divided by: Trailing twelve-month Core EBITDA $ 3,902 Net leverage ratio 1.36x • Liquidity – At the end of the third quarter, the company had $5.0 billion of total liquidity. A transcript of the call will be available on the company’s Investor Relations website at https://ir.cbre.com . About CBRE Group, Inc. CBRE Group, Inc. (NYSE: CBRE), a Fortune 500 and S&P 500 company headquartered in Dallas, is the world’s largest commercial real estate services and investment firm and a premier provider of critical infrastructure services. The company has more than 155,000 employees serving clients in more than 100 countries. CBRE serves clients through four business segments: Advisory (leasing, sales, debt origination, mortgage servicing, valuations); Building Operations & Experience (facilities management, property management, flex space & experience, critical infrastructure); Project Management (program management, project management, cost consulting); Real Estate Investments (investment management, development).
